lines.text: Quick. Memorize this code. Seven. Three. Nine. Two. I'll ask you at the end.
You forget fast. In eighteen eighty-five, Hermann Ebbinghaus memorized nonsense, then tested himself over and over to see how quickly it vanished.
That's the forgetting curve. A steep drop first, then a slow fade. It isn't a flaw. Your brain is deleting whatever never came up again.
But here's the secret. Every time you successfully recall something, the curve gets flatter. The memory lasts longer before it fades.
So the whole game is timing. Review right before you'd forget. Tomorrow. In three days. In a week. In three weeks.
Quick test. Which works better? Reading your notes again, or hiding them and testing yourself? Think!
Testing yourself. The struggle to remember is what builds the memory. Rereading only feels familiar.
So learn it once, then test yourself at one day, three days, one week, and three weeks. Five minutes each. That's the whole system.
Now, the code. Did it survive? Seven. Three. Nine. Two. If you got it, you just proved it. Watch again, and test yourself.
